title: The Terminal gateway passes terminal-api's own 401 and 429 straight to the page: a signed-in user is told to sign in again, and quota refusals have no LIMIT_REACHED code and no Retry-After
root_cause: forward_terminal (apps/edge-bff/app/main.py:541-563) ends with `JSONResponse(status_code=answer.status_code, content=data)`. It returns terminal-api's own status code and flat body ({"error": "<code>", "message"}). M471 mapped edge-bff's own refusals to the CONTRACT section 3 shape but not this relay. A terminal-api 401 is about terminal-api's account or key, never the EDGE session: refuse() for caller kind 'gateway' gives 401 session_ended (terminal-api main.py:312-314, when store.account finds the gateway row inactive or past expires_at), and a wrong key gives 401 proxy_key_rejected (:276-282). terminal-api's quota refusal is 429 quota_exceeded with no Retry-After (take(), :437-439).
evidence: Failing test apps/edge-bff/tests/test_cp0_terminal_relay.py, commit d50893f6. (1) With a valid EDGE session (/api/v1/auth/session 200), an upstream 401 session_ended reaches the page as 401. (2) An upstream 429 reaches the page with no Retry-After and with error == 'quota_exceeded' as a string, not {code: 'LIMIT_REACHED'}. Page side: edge-session.ts:509 `if (res.status === 401) invalidate()`; readError (:321) treats any 401 as kind 'signin'; terminal/src/data/live.ts:80 shows 'Sign in to EDGE first, then open the Terminal tab again.'; watchlist/src/api.ts:44 throws SIGNED_OUT on the relayed reference/logos call. PageFiles maps statuses itself, but its 429 (pages.py:166-167, failure('QUOTA', 429)) also has no Retry-After. test_terminal.py:84 locks the 429 pass-through ('terminal-api's answer passes through'), against CONTRACT section 3.
failure_scenario: Today: the gateway account (terminal.subscriber 2, edge-owner@terminal.local, 'through 2027-10-25', DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md:3587) passes its expires_at or is set inactive. Or TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY is rotated on terminal-api and edge-bff is not redeployed (the M308 class). Then every Terminal, Backtest-preview (/bundle) and Watchlist-logo call answers 401. The shared module drops a valid session, the Terminal asks the user to sign in, and signing in changes nothing. Phase 3c: a per-owner subscriber row that follows a disable gives that owner the same 401. The per-owner D6 quotas (60 tickers/h, 300 files/h) make 429 routine for paid and free users, and they arrive as 'quota_exceeded ... ask the administrator' with no retry_after_s or Retry-After. terminal-api-side refusals (history_days beyond the window) arrive in the flat shape, without details.capability or display_name.
general_class: An upstream service's status code and error body reused as the gateway's own answer, so an upstream account problem looks like the user's session. The same mechanism appears in PageFiles (429 without Retry-After), in the 3c cut relay route still to be built, and in every page that reads /api/terminal/v1: Terminal live.ts, backtest/src/api/live.ts (/bundle), watchlist/src/api.ts (logos). M260 (OPEN) is the same relay lacking public_data, so both belong in one relay helper.
affects_3c_why: 3c makes 401 (per-owner rows that follow a disable) and 429 (per-owner plan quotas) normal answers, and adds terminal-api's own CAPABILITY_REQUIRED for history_days. All of them reach the page only through forward_terminal.
fix: One relay helper for terminal-api answers. A 401 or 403 about terminal-api's account or key becomes 503 TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE in the contract shape, with the upstream code logged. A 429 becomes 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details.limit (terminal-api's quota name), retry_after_s and Retry-After (terminal-api names when the window frees, or a conservative value). terminal-api's capability refusals go out in the contract shape with details.capability and display_name. Apply public_data in the same helper (M260). Change test_terminal.py:84 with the fix (CONTRACT section 3 is the rule).

title: orc-test-runner still holds MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY, the Orc key that may name any owner, so the M475 fix is incomplete at the credential level
root_cause: Phase 0 deploy step 4 left the main key on orc-test-runner 'until a runner suite passes with the test key' (RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md:139-140 and the 'Still open' line :175; EXEC.md:15520). No later entry removes it: the newer entries at the top of RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md (Phase 1 to 3b) never touch orc-test-runner. .railway/railway.ts:36 still declares `MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY: preserve()` beside the test key. M477 says only that run.py reads the test key alone; M475/M477 are marked fixed and deployed, and CONTRACT 8b's 'Open before the switch goes on' does not list this.
evidence: Failing test apps/market-ai-orc/tests/test_cp0_runner_key.py (commit d50893f6): the orc-test-runner env in railway.ts is {'MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY', 'MARKET_AI_ORC_TEST_KEY'}. orc-test-runner is the project's general one-off job box: RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md lists many jobs on it (e.g. :6135, :6278-6351, :6523, :6652), each with a temporary DATABASE_URL. Live variables not read (no Railway access); railway.ts is the config-as-code record of the live project.
failure_scenario: Once EDGE_MULTIUSER is on, any code uploaded to orc-test-runner (a suite, a one-off job, an edited run.py) can read os.environ['MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY']. It can call market-ai-orc with X-Saniti-Owner: u_<any user> and read that user's conversations, messages, run status and exports, stop their runs, or read their progress. That is exactly the cross-owner reach M475's test key (TEST_OWNER_RE) was built to remove.
general_class: A credential retired in code but left in a service's environment. Check every service moved to a narrower key: the workers' TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY now references their service keys (RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md:6871, :6899); AUDIT_STORE_READER_KEY was deleted from orc-test-runner (:3198). For 3c, the terminal-api gateway key must stay on edge-bff only, because with 3c its owner and admin headers are trusted.
affects_3c_why: 3c trusts the terminal-api gateway key, not the Orc key.
fix: Run one runner suite with the test key (needs the user's approval for its cost). Then delete MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY from orc-test-runner, drop it from .railway/railway.ts, and update the M475/M477 status. Until then, list it in CONTRACT 8b 'Open before the switch goes on'.

title: EDGE_OWNER may be set to an owner key Orc reserves for the test key; with the switch off EDGE then runs user #1 under it
root_cause: config.py validate() (:141) checks EDGE_OWNER only against the general shape [A-Za-z0-9._:@-]{1,128}. The reserved list exists in accounts.py reserved_owner and in the users trigger (20261116_003:73), but those only guard server-made keys and the seed row. With the switch off a refused seed is only logged (main.py:248-256, account_seed_failed), and principal.resolve still maps the session to settings.owner (principal.py:298-302).
evidence: Failing test apps/edge-bff/tests/test_cp0_reserved_owner.py (commit d50893f6): validate() raises nothing for golden-suite, test-x, someone-else or default. A probe run then deleted: create_app with owner='golden-x' logged {"event": "account_seed_failed", "error": "CheckViolation"}; sign-in 200; /api/v1/auth/session 200 with access.owner_key 'golden-x'. Orc's TEST_OWNER_RE (conversations.py:55) lets MARKET_AI_ORC_TEST_KEY name exactly such owners.
failure_scenario: An operator sets EDGE_OWNER=golden-main or test-prod (or reuses 'default', Orc's pre-M475 shared owner). EDGE starts normally with the switch off, and every conversation, run, export and manual step of user #1 lives under an owner the test key may read and stop.
general_class: An identity boundary that depends on a key namespace: the reserved-key rule covers server-made keys and DB rows but not the configured key. The same applies to EDGE_ADMIN_OWNERS entries and, in 3c, to terminal.subscriber.edge_owner_key made from the switch-off owner.
affects_3c_why: Production EDGE_OWNER is edge-private per the records, so 3c's owner rows inherit nothing harmful today.
fix: validate() refuses reserved_owner(owner) and 'default' (and the same for EDGE_ADMIN_OWNERS entries), with a message naming the reserved forms and an example (edge-private).

title: The EDGE gateway's terminal-api account expires 2027-10-25 and nothing tracks the date; at expiry every Terminal call fails, and through the relay above it looks like a sign-out
root_cause: The gateway subscriber is a 'person' row with an expires_at ('through 2027-10-25', DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md:3587). store.account() only accepts `active AND expires_at > now()`, and refuse() answers 401 session_ended for the gateway. The service accounts were made with 2100-01-01 (20261028_100:63-67). The date appears nowhere else in the repository (no reminder, check or test).
evidence: grep finds '2027-10-25' only in DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md:3587. store.py account() filters on expires_at > now(). main.py:312-314 refuses a gateway with 401. The live value was not read (no database access).
failure_scenario: On 2027-10-25 every /api/terminal/v1 call (Terminal, Backtest preview, Watchlist logos) answers 401, and through the relay finding above the page says 'Sign in to EDGE first'. The Radar, Overview and Watchlist page files answer 503 UNAVAILABLE. In 3c the admin principal ('admin: true') keeps using this row's limits, so it stays a single point of failure.
general_class: A time-limited row holding up a service credential, with no expiry monitoring. 3c's per-owner rows will need an expiry policy too (from the EDGE plan, not a fixed date).
affects_3c_why: 3c keeps the gateway row as the admin's account and makes per-owner rows whose expiry rule is not yet specified.
fix: With the user's approval, set the gateway row's expires_at to 2100-01-01 like the service accounts (terminal-api admin API, audited). Specify in 3c that owner rows never expire on their own (EDGE's plan decides). Optionally a check that warns 30 days before any key account expires.
confirm_check: Read-only job: SELECT subscriber_id, active, expires_at FROM terminal.subscriber WHERE email = 'edge-owner@terminal.local'.

title: PageFiles' shared caches mean 3c's per-owner terminal-api audit and quota would record only the first owner to read each page file
root_cause: PageFiles asks terminal-api for a grant only when its process cache lacks the file's sha (pages.py:160-178, self.bodies), and the index is shared for 30 s. CONTRACT 3c (:561-563) says PageFiles sends x-terminal-proxy-owner and x-terminal-capabilities so that 'usage and audit are per owner'. With the caches, the owner header reaches terminal-api only on a miss.
evidence: pages.py:160-178. test_radar.py:137-144 locks 'no new grant' for a second read of the same sha. CONTRACT.md 3c 'Caller.credential becomes ('gateway', owner_key), so usage and audit are per owner'.
failure_scenario: After 3c, owner A reads radar-days (grant and access_log row under A); owners B..N read the same file later with no terminal-api call. terminal.access_log shows only A, B's quota is never charged, and a Phase 4 admin reviewing per-user access sees wrong attribution. No data leaks: the capability check runs before the cache (3a).
general_class: A shared process cache in front of a per-principal audit or quota. The same question applies to any 3c cut cache in edge-bff and to the screener and backtest caches if per-owner terminal-api audit is extended to them.
affects_3c_why: 3c specifies the owner header on PageFiles but leaves the shared caches as they are.
fix: Decide in the 3c spec. Either edge-bff records page-file reads per owner itself (or terminal-api gets a cheap audit-only call), or CONTRACT 3c states that page files are audited and counted only on first fetch per process.
confirm_check: After 3c: two principals fetch the same page file; count terminal.access_log rows per edge_owner_key.

title: CONTRACT section 7's Phase 3 Orc capabilities header (X-Saniti-Capabilities: levels, modes, lane, export) is neither built nor recorded as deferred
root_cause: Section 7 (:228-230) says that in Phase 3 edge-bff sends X-Saniti-Capabilities, and that Orc's resolve_model_choice, routed() and lane check use it. 8b D1 defers only the usage ledger, the daily cap and per-plan AI data access, and says the Monitor parts of 3a are 'only the route gates and the model checks'. Reasoning levels, the fast lane, modes and export are not mentioned as deferred.
evidence: grep finds X-Saniti-Capabilities only in CONTRACT.md. client.py:63-65 forwards reasoning_level and lane unchecked. monitor.py gates only monitor.model:<id> and admin.manual.
failure_scenario: When the AI opens to a paid plan, a builder following 8b gates the model only. A paid user could then choose reasoning 'max', the fast lane or exports with no capability, because section 7 is the only place that names them and nothing marks it open.
general_class: A contract clause superseded by a later decision without a record, so the later phase's spec silently drops it.
affects_3c_why: The Monitor is admin-only (D1); 3c does not touch Orc.
fix: Record under D1 in 8b that the Orc capabilities header (levels, modes, lane, export) is deferred with the ledger until the AI opens to a paid plan, or remove it from section 7.

title: F3: an MFA-passed re-enrolment drops confirmed_at, so a password-only session can enrol its own authenticator and take the admin's second factor
root_cause: FlowStore.enroll (auth_flows.py:317-325) overwrites the one mfa_totp row in place: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET nonce=EXCLUDED.nonce, confirmed_at=NULL, last_step=NULL, and deletes every recovery code. mfa_enroll (auth_flows.py:528-534) refuses a pending (password-only) session only when `current['confirmed_at'] and not p.mfa_ok`. So once an MFA-passed session starts a re-enrolment, the account has no confirmed factor until the new one is confirmed, and the rule 'a password alone never resets the second factor' (docstring at :530-531, test_auth_flows.py:518-519) no longer holds.
evidence: tests/test_cp1a_phase1_auth_check.py::test_cp1a_f3_a_password_alone_cannot_enrol_while_a_reenrolment_waits fails on 93c9f645: the thief's POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll answers 200 with otpauth_uri, secret and 10 recovery codes. A control probe (not committed) carried it through: after the admin's re-enrolment confirmed_at is NULL; the thief enrols (200), verifies its own code (200, access.mfa_ok true) and reads an MFA-gated route (GET /api/v1/terminal/layouts 200; GET /api/v1/dev/manual/steps reached the handler). Then the real admin's original authenticator answers 400 MFA_CODE_INVALID, its recovery codes are gone, and its own password-only enrolment is refused 403 MFA_REQUIRED. scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py:36 only resets counts and locks, and a password reset only clears counts (auth_flows.py:283-285), so the real admin has no way back.
failure_scenario: Switch on. The admin (MFA passed) starts setting up a new phone (POST /mfa/enroll) and leaves before confirming, or someone holding a stolen MFA-passed cookie calls enroll. Anyone who knows the admin password signs in (pending session), calls /mfa/enroll (allowed: confirmed_at NULL), confirms with an authenticator of their own and holds an admin session with '*'. The real admin is locked out of the second factor with no operator path back.
general_class: A security setting replaced in place before its replacement is proved, so the old guarantee lapses when the change starts. Same mechanism to avoid in: the email change (purpose email_change exists in email_codes; Phase 4) if the old address is unlinked before the new one is confirmed; recovery-code regeneration; Phase 4/5 admin actions that end the old subscription or role row before the new one is active. Starting a factor change also needs a fresh proof of the current factor (OWASP MFA cheat sheet), which no route asks for today.
affects_3c_why: Phase 3c reads the principal of a valid session; the enrolment decides who gets an admin session, not how a principal is resolved or forwarded to terminal-api. A thief's admin session would carry admin:true in 3c's header, but 3c's code does not build on the enrolment.
fix: Keep the confirmed enrolment (nonce, last_step, recovery codes) while a re-enrolment waits: store the new nonce and recovery codes in a pending slot (new columns or rows, a forward migration), swap them only when a code of the new secret is verified, and refuse /mfa/enroll from any session that has not passed MFA whenever a confirmed enrolment exists. Require a current TOTP or recovery code (step-up) to start a re-enrolment.

title: F2: password/reset answers 429 LIMIT_REACHED after 20 wrong codes only for an address that has an account (enumeration oracle)
root_cause: FlowStore._check_code (auth_flows.py:160-178) returns ('invalid', None) for an unknown address without counting anything (:163-165), and counts CODE_USER only under the existing account's user_id (:166-168, :177). reset (auth_flows.py:269-278) looks up only active accounts, so the 20-per-day cap and its 429 (code_refusal, :420-424) can be reached only for an address that has an account.
evidence: test_cp1a_f2_reset_answers_alike_for_an_account_and_an_unknown_address_after_many_wrong_codes fails on 93c9f645: 21 resets with a wrong code end [..., 400, 400, 429] for ana@example.com (account) and [..., 400, 400, 400] for nobody@example.com. CONTRACT 4 'Enumeration' and 13.4 'identical answers for existing and new emails' are tested only for register (test_auth_flows.py:177-199).
failure_scenario: Switch on. An unauthenticated client sends 21 POST /api/v1/auth/password/reset with any code for a list of addresses; every address whose 21st answer is 429 has an active account. As a side effect each probed account's own codes are refused for 24 h.
general_class: A per-account limit that answers only when the account exists. The sign-in avoids it by counting every typed login (SIGNIN_LOGIN); register, forgot and code/resend answer the same 202 inside their limits; register/verify needs the registration cookie. To keep in mind for every later unauthenticated route with a per-user limit: the email change (Phase 4), an admin 'resend a code', payment flows by email (Phase 5).
affects_3c_why: Account enumeration on the reset route; Phase 3c does not read codes, throttles or reset state.
fix: Count failed reset tries by the normalised address (HMAC key) whether or not it has an account, and decide the 429 from that count, so every address reaches the same 429 after 20 wrong tries; keep the per-user count for registered codes as now.

title: F8: anyone who types a login can keep it at the sign-in limit; a reset by email code does not lift it, a stranger can also kill the live reset code and use up the reset emails, and the message promises a one-minute wait
root_cause: Phase 0 replaced the per-IP limiter (5 per minute; main.py at 83ca29d4) with SIGNIN_LOGIN = 10 per login per 15 min (throttle.py:30), decided before the password check (throttle.attempt, :68-81; main.py:599-602), so the right password is refused too while the typed login is at its cap; SIGNIN_IP stays unenforced (throttle.py:31) because the Railway address probe has not been run (EXEC.md 15584). Nothing lifts the count but a successful sign-in (main.py:634): FlowStore.reset (auth_flows.py:269-287) proves the mailbox but does not clear it. The way back is itself open to a stranger: each password/forgot consumes the live reset code (_issue_code, :149-152) and counts toward the address's 10 emails a day (_may_send/_send, :137-147). The refusal text says 'Wait a minute' (errors.py:18; edge-labels.js:20, :208) while details.retry_after_s is up to ~960 s and the page never reads it.
evidence: test_cp1a_f8_a_password_reset_by_email_code_lets_the_account_sign_in fails on 93c9f645: after 10 wrong tries by a stranger on 'ana_putri' and on 'ana@example.com', the reset answers 200 {"next":"sign_in"} and the sign-in with the new password answers 429 SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT, retry_after_s 931. Probes (not committed): with the switch off, 10 wrong tries on login 'owner' from one client make the owner's correct sign-in from another client 429 (retry_after_s 904); a stranger's forgot turned the owner's emailed reset code into 400 CODE_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED; after 10 stranger forgot calls the owner's own forgot mailed nothing (10 emails before and after).
failure_scenario: Switch off (live on dev now): anyone on the internet who guesses the login (on dev 'edge') sends 10 sign-in requests per ~15 min with the right Origin header; once the owner's 24 h session ends the owner cannot sign in for as long as this continues, being told to 'wait a minute'. Switch on: the same for any account by username and email; the reset says next: sign_in but the sign-in stays refused, and the attacker can also kill each reset code within 60 s and use up the 10 reset emails a day, so the account has no way in.
general_class: A limit keyed by a public identifier that anyone can drive to its cap, with no proof-based way out, and whose message understates the wait. Instances: SIGNIN_LOGIN (switch off and on), CODE_USER through reset (20 wrong codes lock an account's codes 24 h, contract-chosen), SEND_EMAIL and the one-live-code rule through forgot. The MFA lock has ways out (N2). Phase 3c's per-owner Terminal quotas are keyed by the session's owner_key, not a typed value, so they are not in this class.
affects_3c_why: Sign-in availability; 3c starts after a principal exists and keys its quotas by owner_key from the session.
fix: User decision on the way back, then: (1) a reset proved by the email code clears SIGNIN_LOGIN for the account's username and email; (2) run the Railway client-address probe and key the enforced limit by (login, client address) with a looser per-login cap (NIST 800-63B-4 3.2.2 lists IP allowlisting and risk signals for exactly this); (3) forgot within a live code's life re-sends or keeps that code instead of replacing it; (4) the message and the page say the wait from retry_after_s, not 'a minute'.

title: F1: throttle keys '<prefix>:<value>' share a scope with caller-typed keys: the login 'change:<user_id>' locks that user's password change, and the address 'register:<email>' uses up <email>'s new-registration limit
root_cause: Throttle.key_hash (throttle.py:64-66) separates keys only by scope. password_change counts under SIGNIN_LOGIN (scope signin_email) with key 'change:<user_id>' (auth_flows.py:508-511), the scope the sign-in fills with normal_login(typed login) (main.py:599-600, throttle.py:47-49). REGISTER_HOUR/REGISTER_DAY use scope send_email with key 'register:' + email (auth_flows.py:193-196, throttle.py:41-42), the scope SEND_EMAIL fills with the bare address (:146), and checked_email accepts a ':' in the local part (accounts.py:26).
evidence: test_cp1a_f1_a_typed_login_cannot_lock_another_accounts_password_change fails: after 10 unauthenticated sign-ins with login 'change:<ana's user_id>', ana's change with the right current password answers 429 SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT (retry_after_s 940). test_cp1a_f1_another_address_cannot_use_up_the_new_registration_limit_of_an_address fails: after one registration of 'register:vic@example.com', the first ever registration of vic@example.com mails nothing (outbox []); a control with 'other:vic@example.com' mails vic its code.
failure_scenario: Switch on. user_id is a sequential identity, so 10 sign-ins per 15 min per id with login 'change:<id>' keep every account's password change refused. A registration of 'register:<victim>' plus its resends keeps the victim's registration silently dropped all day without one email reaching the victim.
general_class: Domain separation by string prefix inside a shared HMAC scope, where another route feeds caller-chosen text into the same scope. Same scope sharing today: CODE_USER ('<user_id>') and MFA_USER ('mfa:<user_id>') in code_user (safe now, neither takes typed text). Any later limit added to an existing scope with a prefix (Phase 4 admin actions, Phase 5 payments) inherits it.
affects_3c_why: edge-bff sign-in and email throttles only; 3c's quotas live in terminal-api's terminal.quota keyed by owner.
fix: Give each Limit its own label inside the HMAC message (key_hash(scope, label, key)), or its own scope (the migration's CHECK lists scopes, so a forward migration), so no typed value can produce another limit's key.

title: F4: registering again in the same browser within the hour replaces the registration cookie, so the code already mailed can no longer finish the first registration
root_cause: The register route always mints and sets a new registration cookie (auth_flows.py:446-449), also when FlowStore.register made nothing because of the 60 s gap or REGISTER_HOUR/DAY (:188-195). The code activates only the row whose registration_hash equals the cookie's hash (_registration, :208-214), so the browser now holds a cookie naming nothing. code/resend with that cookie answers 202 and sends nothing (:248-254). This is the N3 class of M478, fixed for the sign-in 401 (restart_registration, :376-390) but not for register itself.
evidence: test_cp1a_f4_a_second_registration_in_the_same_browser_keeps_the_first_verifiable fails: after register twice in one client (one email in the outbox), verify with the mailed code answers 400 CODE_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED.
failure_scenario: Switch on. A person registers, goes back to fix a field and sends the form again (the page's busy flag stops only a double click, index.html:11708). The server changes nothing, the shown code fails, and Resend sends nothing; the only way out is to know to sign in with the new password (the restart path).
general_class: An answer that always sets a fresh binding cookie when it made nothing orphans the browser's live binding. Instances: register (open), sign-in 401 (fixed N3). Later browser-bound flows (Phase 5 checkout return) must keep the held binding the same way.
affects_3c_why: Registration only.
fix: When register makes no row, set again the browser's own registration cookie if it names a pending row of the same address (only its holder learns that its own row exists, so no enumeration); otherwise a new unused one as now.

title: F5: USERNAME_TAKEN uses none of the code's 5 tries, so one proved code looks up any number of usernames
root_cause: verify_registration returns ('taken', None) right after _check_code answered 'ok' (auth_flows.py:223-228), with the code still live and neither its attempts nor CODE_USER raised; each try may name another username (register_verify, :455-459).
evidence: test_cp1a_f5_one_code_cannot_look_up_unlimited_usernames fails: one code answers [409, 409, 409, 409, 409, 409] for six taken usernames.
failure_scenario: Switch on. A registrant with an address they control proves one code and then, for 300 s, asks about as many usernames as requests allow (no per-IP limit is enforced), with new codes every 60 s and new addresses at will: a list of valid usernames, each a sign-in login for password spraying.
general_class: A gate whose proof is checked but not counted per answer. The contract puts USERNAME_TAKEN behind the code to stop enumeration; the same applies to any later availability answer behind a code (an email change to a taken address, Phase 4).
affects_3c_why: Registration only.
fix: Count a USERNAME_TAKEN answer as one of the code's tries (attempts+1, consumed at 5), so the code owner may still choose another name a few times.

title: F6: one registration by another browser plus its resends uses all 10 of the address's daily emails, against the recorded decision N4
root_cause: N4 (ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md:9037-9042) bounds new registrations (REGISTER_HOUR/DAY, auth_flows.py:193-196), but resend (purpose register, :241-255) and the sign-in restart (:257-267) of a registration made by another browser are bounded only by _may_send (60 s gap and SEND_EMAIL 10 a day, :137-143), which the address owner shares.
evidence: test_cp1a_f6_registrations_by_others_use_at_most_three_of_the_addresss_daily_emails fails: the victim registers (1 email), an hour later another browser registers the same address and resends 9 times; the outbox then holds 10 emails for the address and the victim's own resend adds none.
failure_scenario: Switch on. Someone registers your address after you and resends once a minute; your code expires after 5 minutes and your resends silently send nothing for a day. N4's stated premise ('registrations by others can then use at most 3 of the address's 10 daily emails') is false.
general_class: A per-address send budget shared between the address owner and anyone who names the address: registration resends and restarts (here) and password/forgot for an existing account (see F8's probe).
affects_3c_why: Email budget of registration only.
fix: Count resends and restarts of a registration under the address's REGISTER limits too (or give each pending registration a small resend budget inside the address budget), or correct the N4 record to state the real bound; a user decision either way.

title: F7: the sign-in body caps login at 200 characters while registration accepts emails of up to 254
root_cause: Login.login has max_length=200 (main.py:109-111), unchanged from the switch-off form; checked_email accepts up to 254 (auth_flows.py:96-100; accounts.py:26 regex allows 64+1+189+1+63).
evidence: test_cp1a_f7_an_account_signs_in_with_any_email_registration_accepted fails: an account registered with a 215-character email answers 422 INVALID_INPUT details.fields ['login'] on sign-in with that email.
failure_scenario: Switch on. A person with a long address registers and verifies, then cannot sign in with the address the page asks for; only the username works, and the refusal says the login field is invalid.
general_class: Two validators of one value with different bounds; check every field the registration accepts against the sign-in, reset and later admin forms (username 30, email 254, password 256 normalised vs 1024 raw, which errs the safe way).
affects_3c_why: Sign-in input only.
fix: Login.login max_length 254 (the registration bound).

title: F9: the route-walk test accepts a hook route listed in HOOK_ROUTES whether or not its handler verifies the signature
root_cause: problems() checks only `callable(registry.get(route.path))` for a hook path (test_route_table.py:58-61); the verifier in HOOK_ROUTES (hooks.py:18) is never tied to the handler, while CONTRACT 6 says the test 'refuses any other route under that prefix without a signature check'. The Origin check skips the whole prefix (main.py:342).
evidence: test_cp1a_f9_the_route_walk_refuses_a_hook_whose_handler_never_checks_the_signature fails: a planted POST /api/v1/hooks/example registered with svix_verify but never calling it accepts an unsigned body with no Origin (200, state changed) and problems() reports nothing. Today's one hook (auth_flows.py:593-609) does verify, and test_auth_flows.py:668 checks it.
failure_scenario: Phase 5 adds POST /api/v1/hooks/payments/{provider}; its handler forgets to verify (or verifies after reading); the route walk stays green and a forged unsigned payment event from anywhere activates a plan.
general_class: A registry membership check standing in for a behavioural guarantee. The payment hooks (CONTRACT 11) are the next routes under the prefix.
affects_3c_why: Hook routes only; 3c adds none.
fix: Make membership imply verification: a dependency built from HOOK_ROUTES verifies request._body before the handler runs and the walk requires that dependency on every hook route; or the walk posts an unsigned body to each hook and requires 401 HOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID with nothing changed.

title: F10: no consecutive-failure cap per account for the password (NIST SP 800-63B-4 3.2.2: at most 100), while the MFA got one
root_cause: The sign-in enforces only SIGNIN_LOGIN, 10 per typed login per 15 min (throttle.py:30; main.py:599-602), cleared by a success (main.py:634); SIGNIN_IP is recorded only (throttle.py:31). An account answers to both its username and its email, so it takes 20 tries per 15 min, about 1,900 a day, with no account-level count across windows. M478 C1 P1-M2 applied the NIST 100-consecutive rule to the TOTP; the same SHALL covers passwords (800-63B-4 3.1.1.2 refers to 3.2.2), and the minimum length is 8 rather than 15 (recorded user decision).
evidence: Code inspection: the only calls at sign-in are throttle.attempt(SIGNIN_LOGIN, login_key) and throttle.count((SIGNIN_IP, ...)) (main.py:600, :625); grep finds no per-account failure counter in accounts.py, throttle.py or the users/identities tables (migrations 20261116_003, 20261117_002). No committed test: the expected behaviour needs the user's decision (see fix).
failure_scenario: Switch on, before the per-IP limit is enforced: a non-admin account with an 8-character password not in Pwned Passwords takes about 1,900 guesses a day, indefinitely, through its username and email.
general_class: Rate limit per identifier but no bound per subscriber account across identifiers and windows; any later login identifier (Google identity, CONTRACT 1) adds another window.
affects_3c_why: Sign-in strength only.
confirm_check: Probe: 101 wrong sign-ins spread past the 15-minute windows (shift auth_throttle.window_start back), then the right password: today 200; under NIST it is refused until a way back (F8 fix 1) is used.
fix: User decision, together with F8: a consecutive-failure count per account (both identifiers), at most 100, cleared by a success or a reset by email code, so the cap never becomes a lock-out without a way back.

title: The Screener's cached paint shows the last result after the plan lost the Screener (and never asks when the plan only narrowed)
root_cause: The boot pointer (scr.boot plus the result bytes in IndexedDB terminal-files) is keyed by the login only (boot-cache.ts:46-50, `if (p.login !== login) drop`). Nothing ties it to the plan (the access.version / X-Edge-Entitlements). app.ts bootPage draws it after the session answer (S3, app.ts:280-285). Every signed-in principal gets that answer, whatever its plan. When the catalog is then refused, the cached catalog stays and only ctx.runError is set (app.ts:290: `if (!ctx.catalog) bootFailed(...) else { ctx.runError = ...; refresh('results') }`). results.ts:166 draws the rows under a note whenever rows exist. When the catalog still answers (a narrowed plan whose filtered catalog is unchanged, a 304), go() sends no run at all for a cached result at the catalog's versions (run.ts:155), so the server never gets to refuse the definition.
evidence: Probe apps/edge-bff/screener/tests/smoke/c_p1s_plan_refused_cache.mjs (smoke build, fixture API). Step 1: the Golden Cross preset is run and cached (7 rows). Step 2: the same login opens the page again with `?fail=catalog:CAPABILITY_REQUIRED:403:9,run:CAPABILITY_REQUIRED:403:9`. Output: "the page still shows 7 rows of the cached last result (before: 7)"; exit 1. The live client behaves like the fixture: live.ts:52-57 (session) and :96 (catalog), where a 403 becomes a thrown ApiFailure. The no-run path is the designed behaviour, proved by the existing smoke step 'cached paint: a second open of the same publication gets 304s and runs nothing'.
failure_scenario: A paid user screens on a metric, then the plan is lowered (D5: a lowered plan loses read access until it is raised again), or narrowed to one without that item. On the next open of the Screener tab in the same browser, the last screen's rows (tickers, prices, metric values) are drawn from IndexedDB. With the plan narrowed and the catalog unchanged, they are drawn as up to date and no request is made.
general_class: A browser copy of an answer computed under a principal's entitlements, read again on the strength of the session (or the login) alone instead of on an answer the current plan earned. Every such cache must be keyed by the entitlements version as well as the identity, or confirmed by a gated answer before it is drawn. The Terminal's file cache is safe: it reads only the shas that /bundle announces on that load (rack.ts announced/readVerified), so 3c's cut files are not built on this. The same class: `edge.watchlist.logos` (class browser) keeps the content of the `logos` reference file, the ticker list, for 12 h. It survives sign-out and a change of user, and the Watchlist reads it before asking (watchlist/src/api.ts:55-60); 3c puts reference files behind `reference`. Any first-paint cache that 3c or 3e adds for the Terminal, including the example mode, falls in it too.
affects_3c_why: The Terminal data path never draws a cached file that the current answer did not announce (sha-keyed, readVerified). 3c's builders should still not add a login-keyed first-paint cache, and 3e's example mode must not boot this BootCache for a principal without screener.view.
fix: Store the session answer's access.version in the BootPointer and drop the pointer when it differs (BootCache.read(login, version)). Alternatively, draw the cached result only after the catalog's own 200/304 for this principal, and drop it on a refused catalog (clear ctx.R and the rows, show the refusal). Make the probe pass, and add a narrowed-plan case once the fixture session carries a version.
confirm_check: cd apps/edge-bff/screener && npx vite build --mode smoke && node tests/smoke/c_p1s_plan_refused_cache.mjs (exit 0 after the fix)

title: /api/v1/preferences serves and stores the tabs' saved items with no tab capability (D5 bypass through Phase 1's preference store)
root_cause: Contract 4b puts the registry's `sync` keys on the server, and it calls them "preferences or saved items": ml.my (Backtest My conditions), scr.last and scr.extraCols (Screener), edge-model-choice (Monitor), edge.watchlist.view, and the Terminal layout keys. The routes need only the principal: preferences.py:119-120 (GET, auth.principal) and :125-126 (PUT, auth.writer). The key is checked for shape only (KEY regex), so neither route asks for the capability of the tab whose data the key holds. Phase 3a's route walk and D5 ("Reads need <tab>.view or the item's own capability, writes need the run or save capability") never covered this route.
evidence: tests/test_c_p1s_preferences_plan.py, run on cluster r1s. A paid user PUTs ml.my and scr.last (201). The subscription is cancelled, so the default plan applies. GET /api/v1/backtests and GET /api/v1/screener/items both answer 403 (D5 holds on the tabs). Yet GET /api/v1/preferences still returns {'ml.my', 'scr.last'}: `AssertionError: ... assert 'ml.my' not in {'ml.my', 'scr.last'}`. The test's next assertion covers the write side: a PUT of ml.my is accepted with no backtest.run.
failure_scenario: A user's plan is lowered. Every Backtest and Screener route refuses them (D5), but GET /api/v1/preferences still hands back their Backtest My conditions and last Screener definition. The shell loads them into localStorage at every sign-in, and the account can keep writing them. That is a second path to the content D5 locks (13.7: 'refused on every second path to the same content').
general_class: A route that reads or writes another tab's data needs that tab's capability, the M481 C2 1 lesson (the Screener star writing the Watchlist). A generic per-account key/value store carries data of every tab. Which capability a key needs is decided by the key, not by the route, so the registry entry should name its tab and the server should check it per key on GET (filter) and PUT (refuse). The same mechanism applies to any later generic store, such as an admin or usage store.
affects_3c_why: The Terminal keys in the store (ml.symbol, ml.assets.v1, the layout keys) are the user's own settings, not market data, and 3c refuses tickers and datasets on the data paths. The store does not widen 3c's data access.
fix: Give each `sync` registry entry its tab, mirrored server-side (a map key -> view/run capability). GET leaves out the keys whose view capability the principal lacks. PUT refuses them with 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED and display_name, so the client's first-sign-in upload skips them. The user could instead decide that preferences stay readable after a downgrade; then record that decision in CONTRACT 4b/8b and move the test to verification/edge_multiuser/access_tiers/pending/.

title: A drawings refusal (403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED) is read as 'account unreachable': the drawing is kept in the browser and the message names a connection failure
root_cause: accountDrawings.listOf maps every failure of GET /api/v1/terminal/drawings to null (drawingsApi.ts:63, `() => null`), which is M468's offline case. load() then says 'could not be saved to your EDGE account just now ... move to the account when it can be reached' (:85). save() keeps the drawing in localStorage stamped with the identity (:130-131, keepCopy), and ownCopy shows it again on every later load. Phase 3a made those routes refuse without terminal.drawings, and the free plan holds none (CONTRACT 9).
evidence: terminal/tests/data/c_p1s_drawings_plan.test.ts. Every drawings route answers 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED (capability terminal.drawings). After load and save, the only message is 'Your drawings could not be saved to your EDGE account just now: they are kept in this browser...'. A scratch variant of the same test showed ml.drawings.BBCA = {"owner":"owner:u_ccc...","drawings":[{"id":"d1",...}]} kept in the browser.
failure_scenario: With the switch on, a free account (no terminal.drawings) draws on the Terminal. Every server call is refused, yet the drawings persist in its browser and show on every reload. The page tells the user the connection failed and to wait, never that the plan lacks drawings (AGENTS.md Gates and evidence (d)). After an upgrade, the local copy merges into the account.
general_class: An offline or fallback path that treats a plan refusal like a network failure and carries on locally. Each client fallback must tell CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, PLAN_EXPIRED and LIMIT_REACHED (403/429, isAccessRefusal) apart from status 0/5xx. Layouts and presets do (savedClient's sentence uses accessText); the drawings' listOf does not. Contract 8b 3e lists lock prompts for Flow, Broker, the indicator menu, compare and assets, but not drawings, so 3e as written would miss this. 3c's Terminal data client should keep the same rule for /bundle and /files refusals (live.ts does today).
affects_3c_why: This is the drawings path of edge-bff and the Terminal page (3e), not terminal-api data. 3c's data refusals are shown through live.ts's accessText.
fix: In listOf and write, keep the error. On an access refusal (isAccessRefusal), say its accessText, keep no local copy (drop pending), and report the drawing tools as locked. Only status 0 or 5xx keeps the offline copy. Add drawings to 3e's lock-prompt list.
confirm_check: cd apps/edge-bff/terminal && npx vitest run tests/data/c_p1s_drawings_plan.test.ts

title: Browser-class keys named after the added series' tickers survive sign-out and a change of user
root_cause: The registry classes the prefix `ml.assets.flow.` as `browser` (edge-session.ts:88, 'an added series pane folded or its height'). assets.ts writes `ml.assets.flow.collapsed.${a.ticker}` for every added series when its pane is made (:419, :471, setCollapsed) and `ml.assets.flow.h.${a.ticker}` on a resize (:479). clearUserState keeps browser keys, and nothing removes these keys, not even removing the series. The user decided on 2026-11-16 (EXEC.md EXEC-MU-ACCOUNTS: "bersihkan pada saat logout") that the added series `ml.assets.v1` are account data cleared at sign-out.
evidence: terminal/tests/data/c_p1s_browser_keys.test.ts. After clearUserState({signOut:true}) and after noteIdentity of another account, ml.assets.v1 is gone and ml.stats.w is kept. These remain: ['ml.assets.flow.collapsed.BBRI','ml.assets.flow.collapsed.TLKM','ml.assets.flow.h.TLKM'] (2 tests failing).
failure_scenario: Account A compares BBRI and TLKM and signs out on a shared computer. The next person reads from localStorage which tickers A compared (and folded or resized), although A's list is cleared. B's Terminal also takes A's per-ticker fold and height choices.
general_class: A `browser` key family whose key names carry account content: classification by prefix misses user data in the suffix. Checked the other browser families: ml.stats.*, ml.broker.*, ml.fd.*, ml.win.* (window ids bs/acc/inv/fd), ml.draw.*, edge-sources-open:<fixed UI labels> carry no account content. ml.winst.* holds a chosen broker-window period (dates), which is borderline. Any per-ticker or per-item UI state that 3c or 3e adds (for example a dismissed lock prompt per ticker) belongs to the same class.
affects_3c_why: These are UI keys, not data paths. 3c adds no such key today.
fix: Class `ml.assets.flow.` as user (cache), or keep the per-series pane state inside ml.assets.v1, and remove a series' keys when it is removed. Extend tests/test_storage_registry.py to refuse a `browser` prefix whose callers build the suffix from a ticker or item id.
confirm_check: cd apps/edge-bff/terminal && npx vitest run tests/data/c_p1s_browser_keys.test.ts

title: The two-user acceptance test (CONTRACT 13.3) leaves out several owned kinds and every cross-owner write by id
root_cause: test_two_users_see_none_of_each_others_rows (test_principal.py:340-412) does not check these: B's queued backtest context excludes A's prior_trials and owner_trials; the backtest /events and /cancel routes; exports; branch and pin on A's run; the PUT of a layout, preset or screener item with A's id (the no-overwrite rule, REVISION_CONFLICT with nothing learned); and adding a ticker to A's watchlist list. FakeOrc.request and messages ignore the owner (conftest.py:59), so the routes that rely on Orc alone (the export download) have no edge-bff isolation test. By code reading every one of these is owner-scoped: backtest.py:691-708; main.py:643-655, 672-679 and 694-701; layouts.py:158-162; presets.py:131-135; screener.py:512-517; watchlist.py:246-251; and Orc main.py:854 owned_export.
evidence: Read the test and the routes. No defect was found, so there is no failing test to commit.

general_class: The 13.3 test lists kinds by hand, while the route table already gives every owned route. A route-derived two-user walk (as the 3a route walk derives capabilities) would cover new routes automatically, 3c's included.
affects_3c_why: It is a test gap only. 3c should add its per-owner terminal subscriber rows to the walk.
fix: Extend the 13.3 test with the missing kinds and the PUT-by-foreign-id cases, or derive the walk from app.routes with the owned-id parameters, and make FakeOrc owner-aware.

title: Values Phase 2 accepts, or reads as the most restrictive (limit 0), break the 3c x-terminal-capabilities header: terminal-api answers 400 for every Terminal call of the account
root_cause: Phase 2 checks only the kind of a value, never a domain per capability. The trigger takes any non-negative integer for a limit and any array of strings for a list (003:118-120). valid_value agrees (principal.py:65-68). read_grants turns a malformed limit into 0 (RESTRICTIVE, principal.py:79, 93-94). The 3c wire is narrower: terminal-api takes history_days only as null or 1..36600 and tickers only as ^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$ (entitlements.py:33-35, 135, 138-139). On p3c-int, terminal_access.capabilities copies p.limit straight into the header (terminal_access.py:90-97). It turns a quota of 0 into 429 LIMIT_REACHED (lines 106-110) but has no such case for history_days or for ticker names.
evidence: Probe on p3c-int 7f95aff9, run from a scratch copy of the 3c tree. A principal with terminal.history_days 0, 40000 or malformed ('730', read as 0), or with terminal.tickers ['bbca'], [' BBCA'] or ['BBCA',''], gets a header that edge-bff sends as is. terminal-api's parse_capabilities raises HeaderError on each one, and owner_of answers 400 invalid_owner_headers (terminal-api main.py:320-322). edge-bff relays that body: answered_capability returns None for a 400, so forward_terminal answers JSONResponse(400, data). The message names internal header fields. pages.py PageFiles turns it into 503 UNAVAILABLE. The 0 case is one Phase 2's own test calls the right shape (test_phase2_fix_round.py test_a_value_of_the_right_shape_is_written, ('terminal.history_days','0')). Committed test apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c_p2_terminal_wire_domain.py: it skips on main (no terminal_access.py) and fails 6 of 6 cases on the p3c-int tree.
failure_scenario: An admin sets terminal.history_days 0, or a value above 36600, for a plan or an override, or writes a ticker as 'bbca'. Or a kind change makes the value unreadable, so it reads as 0. Then every /api/terminal/v1 call of that account, and every Overview, Radar or Watchlist file, fails with terminal-api's internal 400 or a 503. The account never gets a named 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED for the one restriction. It also breaks the M480 promise that the RESTRICTIVE value is a usable 'nothing'.
general_class: Phase 2 has one value domain per kind, while each consumer has its own narrower domain, so a value the catalog accepts can be out of range for the wire that carries it. The same mechanism reaches the 3c quota limits: a RESTRICTIVE 0 becomes 429 'try again later' with Retry-After 3600, although waiting does not help. It also reaches any later limit or list a worker or service validates (context.limits for the workers, Phase 3e page limits). Another check: JS and Python truthiness treat 0 and [] like 'no limit' (None). 3c uses `is None` (terminal_access.py:82, 91), but every new consumer must do the same.
affects_3c_why: 3c builds the terminal-api header from p.limit('terminal.history_days') and p.limit('terminal.tickers') for every Terminal and page-file call, so the Phase 2 domain flows straight into a wire that refuses part of it.
fix: (1) In 3c's terminal_access, map every value Phase 2 can hold onto the wire. history_days 0 (including RESTRICTIVE): refuse 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED terminal.history_days before terminal-api, or let terminal-api take 0 as an empty window. A value above 36600: clamp to 36600, which is beyond any published history. A ticker outside the rule: drop it and log it (fail closed per entry). (2) Optionally give the Phase 2 trigger a domain per capability (terminal.history_days 1..36600, terminal.tickers ^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$) with a hint, so the admin sees the rule when writing. Keep (1) anyway, because the read side can still produce 0. (3) Update the Phase 2 test that calls history_days 0 'right' if (2) is chosen.
confirm_check: Copy the test into a p3c-int checkout and run `python3 -m pytest apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c_p2_terminal_wire_domain.py`: 6 failed. The fix round makes all 6 pass.

title: Principal.refusal never answers PLAN_EXPIRED for a list or limit restriction (terminal.tickers, terminal.history_days), which 3c refuses through p.refusal
root_cause: refusal() picks PLAN_EXPIRED only when holds(expired_grants, expired_kinds, capability) is true (principal.py:157-162). holds() knows only '*', flags and item families (principal.py:98-111). A list or limit key is never 'held', so a paid plan that ended returns false here. That plan had no terminal.tickers row (every ticker) and no terminal.history_days row (no limit), so it did allow what is now refused. CONTRACT 8a says: 'PLAN_EXPIRED is the refusal code when a route needs a capability only the expired plan held'.
evidence: On p3c-int, forward_terminal catches check()'s capability_required(TICKERS) or (HISTORY_DAYS) (terminal_access.py:157, 199) and calls refuse_capability, which raises p.refusal(capability) (main.py:562-566, 590-595). Committed test test_c_p2_recheck.py::test_an_ended_plan_without_a_ticker_list_or_history_limit_gives_plan_expired uses a user whose paid plan ended 1 s ago. p.refusal('terminal.dataset:broker') is PLAN_EXPIRED (passes). p.refusal('terminal.tickers') and p.refusal('terminal.history_days') are CAPABILITY_REQUIRED (fail). Run on cluster r2: 1 failed.
failure_scenario: With the switch on, a paid user's plan ends and the account falls back to the free plan. In the Terminal, BBCA's broker data says 'Your EDGE plan has ended. Renew it'. Opening BBRI, or any date older than 730 days, says 'This feature is not part of your EDGE plan. Upgrade the plan'. So one page gives two different reasons for one cause, and 'upgrade' is wrong for a paying customer.
general_class: The refusal API takes a capability key without the item or amount asked. So any restriction whose 'held' depends on a value (a list member, a number within a limit) cannot follow the PLAN_EXPIRED rule. This covers the 3c refusals (tickers, history), the 3a saved-item caps (LIMIT_REACHED for watchlist, layouts, presets, drawings and backtest.queued_jobs after a lapse), the 3c quota and later limits. Also, CONTRACT 8b '3c in detail' says CAPABILITY_REQUIRED for a ticker outside tickers, which contradicts 8a. The contract needs one sentence that settles it.
affects_3c_why: 3c's refuse_capability is the only call site for the Terminal's list and limit refusals, and it relies on p.refusal deciding the code.
fix: Give refusal a way to judge lists and limits, e.g. p.refusal(key, item=None, amount=None). For a list or limit kind, the ended plan 'held' the request when it had no row for the key (no restriction), the item is in its list, or the amount is within its limit. The 3c call sites pass the ticker or the window. Settle the CONTRACT 8b wording ('CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, or PLAN_EXPIRED per 8a').

title: read_grants hands the same RESTRICTIVE list object to every principal with a malformed list value
root_cause: RESTRICTIVE = {'limit': 0, 'list': []} is module-level (principal.py:79). read_grants stores RESTRICTIVE[kind] itself, not a copy (line 94), and account_principal puts it in p.limits (line 209). Principal is a frozen dataclass, but that list is shared and mutable.
evidence: Committed test test_c_p2_recheck.py::test_a_malformed_list_reads_as_a_new_empty_list_for_each_principal. Principal A has a malformed terminal.tickers, and a consumer runs p.limit('terminal.tickers').append('BBRI'). Principal B, another account also with a malformed list, then reads ['BBRI'] (fails today). A valid list is a fresh object per request, from JSON, so only the fail-closed value is shared. No current or p3c-int code mutates it: terminal_access.py:93 builds a new sorted list.
failure_scenario: A later consumer adds to the list it was given, e.g. a benchmark ticker or a merged watchlist. From then on, every account whose list cannot be read gets those tickers, so the fail-closed value widens across accounts for the life of the process.
general_class: A shared mutable default inside a per-request entitlement object. This applies to any list kind added later and to the 3e mirrors. The front-end limit() returns a filtered copy, which is safe.
affects_3c_why: 3c is the first reader of a list capability (terminal.tickers); it is safe today but nothing enforces it.
fix: Store a copy (list(RESTRICTIVE[kind]) or an empty tuple), or make RESTRICTIVE hold immutable values and keep valid lists as tuples in Principal.limits.

title: seed_subscription treats a plan holding '*' = false as the plan that holds every capability
root_cause: The M480 fix round allowed a flag to be false (trigger 003:117; valid_value principal.py:63-64). The seed plan search still counts rows by key only: SELECT DISTINCT plan_key FROM plan_capabilities WHERE capability_key = '*' (accounts.py:176-177), with no value = true. The same row-existence count appears in the verify blocks (003:283, 004:86, and the 3c migration 20261118_002) and in the test helper make_user (test_principal.py:154).
evidence: Committed test test_c_p2_recheck.py::test_the_seed_plan_is_the_plan_whose_star_is_true. With ('<other plan>','*',false) added, seed_subscription returns None and logs account_seed_plan_ambiguous plans=2 (fails today). A temporary probe set the admin plan's '*' to false: seed_subscription still subscribed user #1 to it ('GIVEN admin'), a plan that now grants nothing.
failure_scenario: An operator marks another plan explicitly '*': false, or the admin plan's '*' is turned off. On a fresh environment (no seed subscription yet), user #1 then gets no plan (locked out of every tab once the switch is on), or a plan that holds nothing, instead of the one plan whose '*' is true. Both outcomes are fail-closed but wrong. dev already holds a seed subscription, so it is unaffected now.
general_class: Code that asks 'which plan holds X' by row existence, after flags started to allow false. The same check is needed in the Phase 4 admin page, the payment adapter's plan lookup and every migration verify that counts '*' holders.
affects_3c_why: 3c reads the principal's resolved '*' (capabilities), which honours false; only the seed lookup and verify blocks count rows.

title: Two edge-bff 429 answers lack Retry-After: the page-file quota refusal and the Terminal gateway relay. These are the paths 3c's per-owner Terminal quotas reach the page through
root_cause: CONTRACT section 3 (line 98) says Retry-After is set on every 429, and a plan limit answers 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details.limit and retry_after_s. Two paths break this. (1) PageFiles.page_file answers terminal-api's 429 on a page-file grant as self.failure('QUOTA', 429) (pages.py:166-167). failure() (pages.py:71) builds a JSONResponse with no headers, uses a family code (RADAR_/OVERVIEW_/WATCHLIST_QUOTA) that is not in the section 3 table, and leaves out details when empty. (2) forward_terminal rebuilds every JSON answer of terminal-api as JSONResponse(status_code=answer.status_code, content=data) (main.py:563). Every response header of terminal-api is dropped, so even a Retry-After added there would never reach the page. terminal-api itself raises its quota 429 without the header: error(429, 'quota_exceeded', ...) at terminal-api main.py:439, an HTTPException with no headers.
evidence: Failing tests in commit ed3fc1f5, apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c_p3a_probes.py. test_a_page_file_quota_refusal_sets_retry_after: Radar grant answered 429 gives 429 with headers {content-length, content-type, x-edge-entitlements, cache-control, csp, ...} and no retry-after. test_a_terminal_quota_refusal_relayed_by_the_gateway_sets_retry_after: POST /api/terminal/v1/files, FakeTerminal 429 quota_exceeded, same result. The existing test_terminal.py:84 locks the pass-through of terminal-api's flat body {'error': 'quota_exceeded'}; tests/test_radar.py:123-125 asserts RADAR_QUOTA without the header. Both fail with the switch off as well, so this has been a Phase 0 error-contract gap since then.
failure_scenario: 3c turns on the per-owner quotas of decision D6 (60 tickers per hour, 200 per day, 300 files per hour, 500 MB per day). A paid user who passes one gets terminal-api's 429 through forward_terminal, or a page-file grant 429 through PageFiles. The answer carries no Retry-After and no LIMIT_REACHED or retry_after_s. The page cannot say when to try again (AGENTS.md Gates (b) and (d)), and the shared module's readError(status, data, Retry-After) gets null. Today the gateway account's 1e9 override hides it.
general_class: An edge-bff path that relays or rebuilds another service's refusal (forward_terminal, PageFiles for overview, radar and watchlist, and any 3c relay such as the cut route) drops that service's headers and code, so the contract's 429 rules never reach the page. The same class covers any future relay of a quota refusal (Orc's daily question cap when the AI opens, D1).
affects_3c_why: 3c builds its per-owner quota rows and headers on exactly forward_terminal and PageFiles (CONTRACT 8b 3c 'edge-bff forward_terminal and PageFiles'). The quota refusals of 3c are the 429s these two paths relay.
fix: In forward_terminal, map a 429 to 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details.limit (the quota name terminal-api reports, e.g. files_per_hour) and retry_after_s, and set the Retry-After header: from terminal-api's own header when present, else a conservative default. Have terminal-api send Retry-After on quota_exceeded (3c builder T). Do the same in PageFiles.failure for QUOTA. Update test_terminal.py:84 and test_radar.py:125, which lock the old shape.

title: 3c design gaps on the code it builds on: Terminal data limits bind only the Terminal paths, and PageFiles' owner-free shared caches conflict with per-owner headers, usage and audit
root_cause: (1) context_of sends the workers rights, allow (item ids) and limits {} only (allow.py:57-59), with no tickers, datasets or history_days. The Backtest (signals, jobs, events), the Screener (run, preview, counts, universe) and the page files overview-stocks and watchlist-stocks all serve every ticker's data, history included. 3c's 'Every path filters' (CONTRACT 8b lines 611-615) lists only terminal-api paths. (2) PageFiles handlers discard the principal (page_index(_=Depends(view)), page_file(..., _=Depends(view)), pages.py:127, 135). terminal() sends only the proxy key (pages.py:103-106). The index is cached 30 s and the bytes by sha (self.bodies, 32 MB), both shared by every principal. 3c says PageFiles send x-terminal-proxy-owner and x-terminal-capabilities built from the principal, and that 'usage and audit are per owner' (CONTRACT line 600).
evidence: Code read on 93c9f645 at the lines above. tests/test_phase3a_monitor_pages.py::test_a_page_file_is_refused_even_after_another_account_filled_the_shared_cache shows the second account is served from the cache with no terminal-api call (FakeHttp.calls unchanged), so its read is never granted, counted or audited under its own owner.
failure_scenario: (1) A future plan (or an override) holding backtest.run, screener.run or watchlist.view with terminal.tickers ['BBCA'] or history_days 730 reads every ticker's full history through the Backtest preview, the Screener or the watchlist file, while the Terminal refuses it. (2) After 3c, page-file grants are counted and audited only for the first owner who reads a sha in a process. If terminal-api ever filters a page-family index per owner, the 30 s shared index serves one owner's view to all. And once step 4 (terminal-api requires the headers) lands, the index and grant calls need a principal that the handlers do not pass today.
general_class: A data restriction enforced on one path (the Terminal proxy) while other tabs read the same data through their own workers or files, and owner-free shared caches placed in front of a call that becomes per owner.
affects_3c_why: 3c builds the per-owner headers, quotas and audit on forward_terminal and PageFiles, and claims that every path filters. Both points must be decided and recorded in CONTRACT 3c before the build is checked.
fix: Record in CONTRACT 8b which paths terminal.tickers, terminal.dataset and terminal.history_days bind. Either a plan that restricts them must not hold backtest.*, screener.*, overview.view or watchlist.view (a catalog check or trigger), or edge-bff passes them to the workers and page files. For PageFiles, thread the principal into index() and terminal(), and record that a cached page file is granted, counted and audited once per sha per process, or key the caches per owner.
confirm_check: Contract review by the main agent. For (1), a probe: a paid account with override terminal.tickers ['BBCA'] posts /api/v1/backtests/signals for BBRI, and edge-bff relays it to the worker with no ticker restriction.

title: F2: the workers hard-code their own capability family in CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, but the 3b follow-up (built with 3c) moves the indicator and Flow grants to terminal.* and deletes the backtest.*/screener.* rows
root_cause: The workers build details.capability from constants of their own: backtest-worker access.ts:30-32 (FAMILY, used at :91) and screener-worker run.ts:81-83 (CAPABILITY_FAMILY, used at :183). edge-bff decides the item from app/allow.py:26-31 (FAMILIES) and relays the refusal unchanged, adding only display_name (allow.py named). The CONTRACT '3b follow-up' (8b lines 631-633) changes allow.FAMILIES to terminal.indicator and terminal.flow_indicator. Its forward migration removes backtest.indicator, backtest.flow_indicator, screener.indicator and screener.flow_indicator. 'Worker refusal' (8b line 477) still says capability is 'the family key of that worker, e.g. backtest.indicator:I07', and the follow-up names neither worker constant. Today the two sides agree only because both still say backtest.*/screener.*.
evidence: Failing test apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c_p3b_recheck.py::test_f2_a_worker_refusal_names_the_family_edge_bff_decides_the_item_by (commits 114737d3, 3d75fb1d). It parses both workers' constants, passes the refusal through allow.named, and requires the capability the page receives to equal allow.FAMILIES (passes today) and, per O3b-1, terminal.* for indicator and Flow (fails today). Simulating a follow-up that changes allow.FAMILIES only makes the first block fail: 'the backtest worker refusal reaches the page naming backtest.indicator:<id>, but edge-bff decides its indicator items by terminal.indicator'. After the row removal, errors.display_name (app/errors.py:82-90) finds neither the key nor its family in _names and returns UNNAMED, 'This part of EDGE'.
failure_scenario: After the follow-up and its migration, with the switch on, a paid account whose terminal.indicator excludes I07 runs a backtest with I07. The worker answers 403 with details.capability 'backtest.indicator:I07', a capability that no longer exists and that no admin can grant. display_name becomes 'This part of EDGE: ...' or UNNAMED, and the 3e lock prompt keyed by the capability cannot match the Terminal item. Nothing shows with the switch off, because the configured owner holds '*'.
general_class: Two services name the same decision separately: edge-bff decides the grant, the worker names it in its refusal, and nothing binds the two. The same mechanism applies wherever a refusal is produced by a service other than the one that owns the catalog. In 3c that is terminal-api refusing with terminal.dataset:<id>, terminal.history_days or terminal.tickers, built from a header edge-bff sends. affects_3c_why: The 3b follow-up is built and shipped with 3c and rewires exactly these families. Built as specified, it leaves the workers naming deleted capabilities. 3c's terminal-api refusals have the same two-sided shape.

The deploy order is the workers' CLI upload with step 3, as already planned. Keep this test as the cross-service guard.

title: Column-level privileges pass every grant guard: the $verify$ blocks, provision_edge_bff_login.py and the apply-job probes check has_table_privilege only
root_cause: has_table_privilege is false for a privilege held on columns only. The provisioning script's reachable-relations query (provision_edge_bff_login.py:76) and its exact-grant loop (:87), every migration's $verify$ block, and the runtime_grants/login_grants probes of the apply jobs all use it, so a column grant is invisible to every check.
evidence: Local cluster, all edge_bff migrations applied: `GRANT UPDATE (reason) ON edge_bff.admin_audit TO edge_bff_runtime` and `GRANT SELECT (secret) ON public.mp TO edge_bff_runtime`: has_table_privilege false, has_any_column_privilege true; as edge_bff_runtime `UPDATE edge_bff.admin_audit SET reason='rewritten'` -> UPDATE 1 and `SELECT secret FROM public.mp` -> 'market'. provision_edge_bff_login.py then printed 'EDGE login provisioned; only the 28 operational tables reachable' while edge_bff_login held both. The 20261116_003 $verify$ block re-run on that database passed. DATABASE_CHANGELOG's 'runtime_grants and login_grants equal the expected ones' (Phase 1, Phase 2) is evidence of table-level grants only; column ACLs on dev were never read.
failure_scenario: An operator or a later migration grants a column privilege (e.g. UPDATE (reason) on admin_audit, or SELECT on a column of a market table); every guard and read-back reports least privilege, and edge-bff (or anyone holding its login) can rewrite the audit or read market data.
general_class: Every grant guard in the repository built on has_table_privilege: all edge_bff $verify$ blocks (20261008_002 onwards), the provisioning script, the apply-job probes, and the market-ai reader roles' checks; 3c's new grants (terminal.subscriber column, the edge_bff quota rows) will copy the same pattern.
affects_3c_why: 3c adds a terminal schema migration and an edge_bff migration whose verify blocks and job probes will reuse this has_table_privilege pattern; the check should be fixed before it is copied again.
fix: In the script, the verify blocks and the probes, also fail when has_any_column_privilege(role, table, priv) is true beyond the table grants (or read pg_attribute.attacl IS NOT NULL for the role); one-off read-only check on dev: `SELECT attrelid::regclass, attname, attacl FROM pg_attribute WHERE attacl IS NOT NULL AND array_to_string(attacl, ',') ~ '(edge_bff_runtime|edge_bff_login|=)'`.
confirm_check: tests/test_cdb_grants_and_records.py::test_provisioning_refuses_a_privilege_held_on_columns_only (both cases) and ::test_the_migration_verify_block_refuses_an_audit_column_update; the dev read-back named in fix confirms no column grant exists there today.

title: admin_audit is rewritten by user deletion: its FKs are ON DELETE SET NULL, so the hourly pending-account purge nulls the target of audit rows
root_cause: admin_audit.actor_user_id and target_user_id reference users ON DELETE SET NULL (20261116_003:191,193). Referential actions run as the table owner, so the 'no UPDATE, no DELETE' grant (CONTRACT section 1) does not hold when edge-bff deletes a user: purge_pending (accounts.py:248) and the deletion of other pending registrations (auth_flows.py:237) both do.

Probe test fails with 'the purge rewrote an audit row (target_user_id set to NULL)'.
failure_scenario: Phase 4: an admin resends a code to (or edits) a pending account; 24 h later the purge deletes it and the audit row no longer names whom the admin acted on; the same happens to actor rows if an admin account is ever deleted.
general_class: Provenance columns with ON DELETE SET NULL: user_capability_overrides.created_by_user_id (20261117_003:80) loses who granted an override; Phase 5 payment_events and any audit-like table referencing users will hit the same mechanism.
affects_3c_why: 3c writes no admin_audit row; Phase 4 (admin dashboard) builds on it.
fix: Keep audit user ids without a cascading FK (store the id, or ON DELETE NO ACTION and have the purge skip accounts the audit names), in a forward migration before Phase 4 writes audit rows.

title: A change of the plan catalog leaves no trace: plan_capabilities.updated_at and version are not maintained on UPDATE, and overrides have no updated_at/updated_by
root_cause: plan_capabilities.version and updated_at (20261117_003:66-67) are only column defaults; nothing raises them on UPDATE (the table COMMENT asks the operator to 'raise version with it'). user_capability_overrides is UPDATE-granted but has only created_at/created_by_user_id, so a changed override keeps its creator's name.
evidence: Probe: UPDATE plan_capabilities SET value='365' for free/terminal.history_days left version 1 and updated_at equal to its insert time (assertion 'plan_capabilities.updated_at did not move with the change'). The X-Edge-Entitlements fingerprint still changes (principal.version_of hashes the resolved grants), so access is correct; only the record is missing.
failure_scenario: An operator lowers a plan limit or a 3c quota on dev with a catalog-only UPDATE (CONTRACT 8a 'no restart'); later nobody can tell from the table when the grant changed, and version still says 1, so a review reads the seed's value as untouched.
general_class: Operator-edited data tables without an update trigger or audit: plans, capabilities, plan_capabilities, user_capability_overrides, subscriptions (last_event_at only); 3c adds its Terminal quota rows to plan_capabilities.
affects_3c_why: 3c adds the D6 quota rows (terminal.tickers_per_hour and the others) to plan_capabilities, the rows an operator will tune; their changes would be untraceable.
fix: A forward migration with a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on plan_capabilities that sets updated_at = now() and version = OLD.version + 1 when value changes, and updated_at/updated_by_user_id on user_capability_overrides (or an audit row per change).

title: Three database backstops no test locks: users_registration_pending, the email-code attempts cap, users_one_seed
root_cause: The app logic enforces the same rules (auth_flows._check_code selects attempts < 5; activation clears registration_hash; the owner-key trigger refuses a second non-u_ row), so no test exercises the constraints themselves.
